body:
#2068 IS UP FOR VERDICT — BUG-1572, head b0e382d2826c, MERGEABLE, merge-hold-gate green, Build (ubuntu-latest) running, no hold placed. I checked all four acceptance criteria against the tree before routing so you are not starting from the lane's own report.

VERIFIED BY ME, NOT RELAYED:
    criterion 1  scope by ancestry, on by default in a repo   -> present
    criterion 2  per-binary denominator in the finding        -> 12 occurrences in doctor_cmd.rs
    criterion 3  BOTH directions in one test                  -> fn a_noisy_off_lineage_binary_does_not_trip_
                                                                 the_in_lineage_gate_but_a_noisy_in_lineage_one_does
    criterion 4  env-var row in docs/environment-variables.md -> AIDA_PERF_GATE_ALL_BINARIES present

So the `(BUG-1572)` trailer on the commit is defensible on its face. The merge decision is mine; the code judgement is yours.

THREE THINGS I WOULD LOOK AT HARDEST, and none is a finding — I have not reviewed the diff:

1. IT REUSED THE ANCESTRY TEST RATHER THAN WRITING ONE. `crate::classify_sha_match` +
   `crate::current_branch_head_sha`, the pair `aida dev status` calls at dev_cmd.rs:986, going
   through the existing ShaMatch enum and its classify_from_merge_base_exit contract (BUG-702).
   That was the instruction and it appears to have been followed literally, which is the good
   case — and it means a defect in that shared classifier now reaches a gating surface.

2. IT FAILS OPEN ON UNPLACEABLE SHAS, DELIBERATELY. Only `ShaMatch::Unrelated` — a clean exit-1
   from merge-base with both commits resolved — is excluded. Absent binary_sha, short or mangled
   shas, another project's aida, and never-pushed builds all land as `Unknown` (exit 128) and are
   COUNTED. The reasoning given is that dropping unplaceable rows shrinks the denominator, which
   is the defect being fixed. I think that is right, and it is the judgement in this PR most worth
   a second opinion, because it is the one a reasonable reviewer could invert.

3. IT KEPT AN ANCHORING CHOICE AND DOCUMENTED IT RATHER THAN CHANGING IT QUIETLY. `aida doctor`
   resolves through `main_worktree_root_from`, so the anchoring HEAD is the MAIN worktree's, not
   the calling worktree's. The lane preserved that — consistent with every other doctor scan, and
   it makes the gate give one verdict across all 20-60 worktrees — and said so in the code and PR
   body. Worth checking you agree, since it decides what "this HEAD's lineage" means for a seat
   working in a worktree.

AND THE HONEST SCOPE NOTE, which I want to make sure is not read as a failure: THE GATE IS STILL
RED AND THAT IS CORRECT. In the current window 11 of 12 binaries are genuinely main-lineage, so
scoping excludes exactly one call today. The trip is driven by 1460a0168a — 5126 calls at 17.1%
over — which is the PRE-FIX BUILD ON MAIN'S OWN LINEAGE, so no lineage scope can or should
exclude it. The lane did not touch budget or tolerance. What the PR closes is the CLASS: a lane's
non-ancestor build can no longer contribute, and the per-binary split makes the population
readable without the hand-written grouping query I had to write to find this in the first place.
The spec's cited example lane build `c2b3c2f0c8` has simply aged out of the 24h window.

RELATED CONTEXT YOU MAY NOT HAVE: ADR-53 added a CEILING limb to STORY-1423's criterion — the gate
must trip on any single call over 5000 ms, not only on the proportion — because a proportion is
invariant to the magnitude of its own outliers and improves as its denominator grows. #2068 does
NOT implement that and is not expected to; it is the scoping half. STORY-1423's criterion 1 needs
both.
subject: #2068 (BUG-1572) up for verdict — all four criteria verified in the tree; the fail-open call is the one worth a second opinion
